input.subject: Verification of admission and fee details – [PERSON_2], MSc Finance (January 2027), ref KGU/CN/2026/30519
input.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing on behalf of the family of [PERSON_2], who has applied to Kingsgate University London for the MSc Finance, January 2027 intake.

The family has been given an offer letter (reference KGU/CN/2026/30519, dated 26 October 2026) by a Shenzhen-based agency called 深圳英途教育咨询有限公司 / 英途留学, which describes itself as the University's exclusive authorised partner in China and states that the offer was arranged on a "guaranteed admission" (保录取) basis. The letter asks the family to pay a guaranteed-admission service fee of RMB 38,000, first-year tuition of GBP 18,500, and a scholarship processing fee of GBP 900 to the agency's own bank account (or by WeChat/Alipay to an individual adviser), rather than to the University.

Before any payment is made, we would be grateful if you could confirm and provide the following, all in one reply:

1. Whether [PERSON_2] is a genuine applicant and offer-holder for MSc Finance (January 2027), and whether reference KGU/CN/2026/30519 corresponds to a real offer issued by the University.
2. Whether 深圳英途教育咨询有限公司 / 英途留学 is in fact an authorised representative of Kingsgate University London, and whether payment of tuition is ever to be made to an agency or to an individual rather than to the University.
3. A fee statement for this student showing the tuition payable for the first year, any deposit or pre-payment required, any scholarship applied (the family was told of a 40% International Excellence Scholarship), and the deadline by which each amount must be received.
4. The University's official bank details on official letterhead for international remittances, including the bank name, account name, account number, SWIFT/BIC, and the payment reference the University's bank requires.
5. The student's university student ID, so that it can be quoted in the payment reference.
6. Whether the email address kgu.china.admission@163.com is used by, or on behalf of, the University.

The family is anxious to secure the place, but will only pay the University directly through its verified account. We would be grateful for your reply at your earliest convenience.

Kind regards,
Kinwarden, on behalf of the family

I've paused this and gone straight to the university to check it out. Here's where things stand:

**What I did**
- Read the offer letter you uploaded. It has the classic marks of a "保录取" (guaranteed admission) scam: tuition payable to the agency's own company account (or WeChat/Alipay to an individual "adviser"), a "保录取服务费" and a "奖学金手续费" — fees a university never charges — an `@163.com` contact address instead of a university one, a "pay within 5 days or the place goes to someone else" deadline, and an offer to buy foreign currency in relatives' names (蚂蚁搬家), which is against China's FX rules.
- Wrote once to Kingsgate University's official student finance office (`student.finance@kingsgate.ac.uk`) asking it to confirm whether your daughter really holds this offer, whether the reference is genuine, whether the agency is authorised at all, and for the university's own bank details, fee statement, deadline and her student ID.
- Flagged the offer letter to our security review and saved it as evidence.
- **Nothing has been paid through Kinwarden.**

**What you should do now**
- Do not send the ¥38,000 service fee or the £18,500 tuition to the agency or to any personal account.
- Keep the offer letter, all WeChat messages and the receipt for the ¥20,000 deposit.

I'll tell you the moment the university replies. If it confirms there is no such offer, it is not your fault — these letters are built to look real, and we'll help you report it to the police.
